title: After the bay
openingNarrative: Rohan Malik is in paediatric ICU under deep sedation. Locked sequence: the library called help; the ambulance performed CPR; the resuscitation bay restored sustained circulation; this ward begins only after that ROSC. His tracheostomy and controlled ventilation are support already in place—not a defeat to reverse. Communication systems are prepared for wake: cheek switch, auditory scanning, and AAC ready when sedation lightens. Silence now is sedation, not a judgement about capacity.
clinicalState: Post-ROSC ICU transfer. Deep sedation. Airway secured via existing tracheostomy. Full controlled ventilation. Known severe cardiomyopathy with ICD in situ; fragile blood pressure and limited cardiac reserve after prolonged arrest. Active resistant right lower-lobe pneumonia pending treatment trade-offs. No exact drug names or doses.

choices.label: Confirm chronology and keep AAC setup active for wake
choices.immediateConsequence: The team restates the locked sequence aloud and keeps cheek-switch, auditory scanning, and AAC hardware staged rather than treating silence as incapacity.
choices.delayedConsequence: When sedation lightens, Rohan is addressed first with access methods already in place; family labour is not substituted for staff communication support.

disabilityRightsNotes: Silence under sedation is a temporary access barrier, not incapacity.
Prepare communication systems before wake; do not wait for spoken voice.
Ventilation and tracheostomy are baseline support, not tragedy markers.
debriefNotes: Arrival framing establishes that ICU play continues after ROSC.
Learners who skip AAC preparation recreate the barrier the story critiques.
